newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan seen to tender for U.S. corn/soybeans-trade.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan seen to tender for U.S. corn/soybeans-trade.

text.p: Taiwan is expected to tender for up to 124,000 tonnes of U.S. corn and 38,000 tonnes of soybeans after getting what one dealer called "ideal" prices, traders said on Monday.
"U.S. corn prices are nearing bottom," a buyer with the Members Feed Industry Group said.
The group plans to place a tender for at least one 54,000-tonne corn shipment within the next two weeks, he added.
Hui Shung Group may also place a tender within two weeks for a combined shipment totalling 54,000 tonnes of U.S. corn and soybeans. The shipment is for late March delivery.
The price of the March corn contract on the Chicago Board of Trade (CBOT) ended down two U.S. cents at US$2.56-1/2 a bushel on Friday.
The Taiwan Flour Mills Association will remain on the sidelines of the wheat market this week, association official Lu Wei-chih said.
Domestic soymeal for Taipei delivery was quoted at between T$9.55 to $9.75 a kg, down from the previous T$9.70-$9.80 a kg.
Corn powder was seen at T$6.80-$6.85 a kg for Taipei delivery, down from T$6.95-$7.00 a kg last week.
Flour prices were seen in a range between T$14.55-$15.68 a kg for Taipei delivery, unchanged from the previous week.
Freight rates from the Pacific Northwest were quoted at about US$11.50 a tonne, while Gulf of Mexico rates ranged between $20.50 to $21.50 a tonne, both for Panamax-sized March shipments.
